contribution_review.reason: Selected full-name matched neuroscience papers centered on bat spatial and social neural coding; an unrelated cardiac-regeneration coauthorship was not used.

contributions.value: Bat grid cells without continuous theta oscillations
contributions.summary: Recorded medial entorhinal grid cells in Egyptian fruit bats and found grid-like spatial firing without continuous theta-band oscillations, challenging oscillatory-interference explanations requiring theta rhythmicity.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Michael M Yartsev and colleagues; PubMed author evidence lists Michael M Yartsev as a coauthor. Credit is collaborative and does not imply sole authorship.

sources.title: Grid cells without theta oscillations in the entorhinal cortex of bats.
sources.supports: The paper reports bat entorhinal grid cells without continuous theta oscillations and lists Michael M. Yartsev as a coauthor.

contributions.value: Three-dimensional hippocampal place coding in flying bats
contributions.summary: Used wireless recordings in freely flying bats to show that hippocampal place cells encode confined three-dimensional volumes with similar resolution across axes, supporting a volumetric spatial representation.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Michael M Yartsev and colleagues; PubMed author evidence lists Michael M Yartsev as a coauthor. Credit is collaborative and does not imply sole authorship.

sources.title: Representation of three-dimensional space in the hippocampus of flying bats.
sources.supports: The paper reports 3D hippocampal place coding in freely flying bats and lists Michael M. Yartsev as a coauthor.

contributions.value: Inter-brain neural correlations during natural bat social interactions
contributions.summary: Simultaneously recorded neural activity from pairs of interacting bats and found correlations across brains over seconds-to-hours timescales, with correlation strength linked to social context and interaction extent.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Wujie Zhang and colleagues; PubMed author evidence lists Michael M Yartsev as a coauthor. Credit is collaborative and does not imply sole authorship.

sources.title: Correlated Neural Activity across the Brains of Socially Interacting Bats.
sources.supports: The paper reports simultaneous recordings from socially interacting bats and lists Michael M. Yartsev as a coauthor.

contributions.value: Flexible use of cache memories in food-caching birds
contributions.summary: Designed an automated chickadee caching arena and behavioral models showing that birds combine precise memories of cache-site contents with non-mnemonic strategies such as opportunistic foraging and spatial biases.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Marissa C Applegate and colleagues; PubMed author evidence lists Dmitriy Aronov as a coauthor. Credit is collaborative and does not imply sole authorship.

sources.title: Flexible use of memory by food-caching birds.
sources.supports: The paper reports behavioral apparatus and modeling of chickadee cache-memory use and lists Dmitriy Aronov as a coauthor.

contributions.value: Hippocampal barcodes for episodic cache memories
contributions.summary: Recorded chickadee hippocampal activity during caching and retrieval, revealing sparse barcode-like neural patterns that uniquely marked individual caching events and reactivated during retrieval of the corresponding cache.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Selmaan N Chettih and colleagues; PubMed author evidence lists Dmitriy Aronov as a coauthor. Credit is collaborative and does not imply sole authorship.

sources.title: Barcoding of episodic memories in the hippocampus of a food-caching bird.
sources.supports: The paper reports event-specific hippocampal barcode patterns in food-caching birds and lists Dmitriy Aronov as a coauthor.

contributions.value: Remote gaze activation of hippocampal place codes
contributions.summary: Showed that chickadee hippocampal place cells can activate when the bird gazes at a location from a distance, linking place coding to active visual behavior and remote spatial functions.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Hannah L Payne and colleagues; PubMed author evidence lists Dmitriy Aronov as a coauthor. Credit is collaborative and does not imply sole authorship.

sources.title: Remote activation of place codes by gaze in a highly visual animal.
sources.supports: The paper reports gaze-related activation of hippocampal place codes and lists Dmitriy Aronov as a coauthor.

records.name: Karl Deisseroth

identity.note: Imported roster identity; not independently established.

contribution_review.reason: Selected three distinct, full-name matched primary-paper examples spanning optogenetic control, circuit discovery, and tissue-clearing methods.

contributions.value: Millisecond optogenetic control of mammalian neural activity
contributions.summary: Adapted Channelrhodopsin-2 for temporally precise optical stimulation of mammalian neurons, demonstrating control of single-spike timing and excitatory or inhibitory synaptic transmission as a broadly useful neural perturbation tool.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Edward S Boyden and colleagues; PubMed author evidence lists Karl Deisseroth as a coauthor. Credit is collaborative and does not imply sole authorship.

sources.title: Millisecond-timescale, genetically targeted optical control of neural activity.
sources.supports: The paper reports Channelrhodopsin-2-based millisecond control of mammalian neuronal spiking and synaptic transmission and lists Karl Deisseroth as a coauthor.

contributions.value: Parvalbumin interneuron control of cortical gamma rhythms
contributions.summary: Used optogenetic modulation in mouse neocortex to show that parvalbumin interneurons can suppress or generate gamma-frequency rhythmicity and that gamma-frequency input modulation can improve signal transmission.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Vikaas S Sohal and colleagues; PubMed author evidence lists Karl Deisseroth as a coauthor. Credit is collaborative and does not imply sole authorship.

sources.title: Parvalbumin neurons and gamma rhythms enhance cortical circuit performance.
sources.supports: The paper reports bidirectional optogenetic tests of parvalbumin interneuron roles in gamma rhythms and lists Karl Deisseroth as a coauthor.

contributions.value: CLARITY intact-tissue molecular and structural imaging
contributions.summary: Introduced CLARITY, transforming intact tissue into a transparent, macromolecule-permeable hydrogel hybrid that enabled three-dimensional imaging and molecular labeling across mouse brain and clinical tissue samples.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Kwanghun Chung and colleagues; PubMed author evidence lists Karl Deisseroth as a coauthor. Credit is collaborative and does not imply sole authorship.

sources.title: Structural and molecular interrogation of intact biological systems.
sources.supports: The paper describes CLARITY for intact-tissue structural and molecular interrogation and lists Karl Deisseroth as a coauthor.

contributions.value: Cutaneous LTMR organization of hairy-skin touch
contributions.summary: Genetic labeling showed that guard, awl/auchene and zigzag hair follicles are innervated by invariant combinations of Aβ-, Aδ- and C-LTMRs whose central projections form narrow dorsal-horn columns, supporting a circuit model for diverse touch sensations.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Lishi Li, Michael Rutlin, Victoria E. Abraira and colleagues; the primary paper lists David D. Ginty as a coauthor.

sources.title: The functional organization of cutaneous low-threshold mechanosensory neurons.
sources.supports: LTMR subtype labeling, hair-follicle innervation patterns, dorsal-horn columns, and David D. Ginty authorship.

contributions.value: Cellular and synaptic architecture of the LTMR-recipient dorsal horn
contributions.summary: Mouse genetic tools and circuit analyses defined diverse excitatory and inhibitory interneuron subtypes in the LTMR-recipient zone, showing how LTMR classes, spinal interneurons and corticospinal inputs converge in a complex spinal region for tactile perception.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Victoria E. Abraira, Emily D. Kuehn, Anda M. Chirila and colleagues; the primary paper lists David D. Ginty as a coauthor.

sources.title: The Cellular and Synaptic Architecture of the Mechanosensory Dorsal Horn.
sources.supports: Genetic tools, dorsal-horn neuronal diversity, synaptic input logic and David D. Ginty authorship.

contributions.value: Developmental emergence of somatosensory neuron transcriptional identity
contributions.summary: A developmental single-cell atlas in mice indicated that somatosensory neurons arise from a transcriptionally unspecialized state and diversify as broad transcription-factor expression becomes subtype restricted, with target-derived cues such as NGF helping shape subtype programs.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Nikhil Sharma, Kali Flaherty, Karina Lezgiyeva and colleagues; the primary paper lists David D. Ginty as a coauthor.

sources.title: The emergence of transcriptional identity in somatosensory neurons.
sources.supports: Somatosensory neuron transcriptomic atlas, developmental diversification model and David D. Ginty authorship.

records.name: Gwyneth Card

identity.note: Imported roster identity; not independently established.

contribution_review.reason: Selected full-name Drosophila primary papers spanning escape planning, action selection and descending pathway organization.

contributions.value: Visually mediated motor planning for Drosophila escape
contributions.summary: High-speed behavioral analysis showed that flies use visual information before takeoff to adjust posture and direct jumps away from a looming threat, demonstrating rapid state-dependent motor planning in a genetically accessible organism.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored by Gwyneth Card and Michael H. Dickinson; the primary paper lists Gwyneth Card as first author.

sources.title: Visually mediated motor planning in the escape response of Drosophila.
sources.supports: Visual stimulus-dependent escape postural planning and Gwyneth Card authorship.

contributions.value: Spike-timing mechanism for escape action selection
contributions.summary: Intracellular recordings during looming-evoked escape showed that timing of giant-fiber spikes relative to parallel escape circuits biases flies between longer stable takeoffs and faster unstable takeoffs, linking circuit timing to action selection.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Catherine R. von Reyn, Patrick Breads, Martin Y. Peek and colleagues; the primary paper lists Gwyneth M. Card as a coauthor.

sources.title: A spike-timing mechanism for action selection.
sources.supports: Bimodal escape behavior, giant-fiber timing mechanism and Gwyneth M. Card authorship.

contributions.value: Functional map of Drosophila descending sensory-motor pathways
contributions.summary: A systematic anatomical survey identified roughly half of Drosophila descending neurons, generated more than 100 targeting lines and mapped sensory-to-motor connectivity, revealing layered nerve-cord organization related to walking and flight control.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Shigehiro Namiki, Michael H. Dickinson, Allan M. Wong and colleagues; the primary paper lists Gwyneth M. Card as a coauthor.

sources.title: The functional organization of descending sensory-motor pathways in Drosophila .
sources.supports: Descending neuron anatomy, driver-line resource, connectivity map and Gwyneth M. Card authorship.

records.name: Lisa Giocomo

identity.note: Imported roster identity; not independently established.

contribution_review.reason: Selected full-name entorhinal cortex papers linking cellular physiology, landmarks and mixed navigational codes.

contributions.value: Subthreshold oscillation frequency linked to grid-cell spacing
contributions.summary: In vitro recordings from entorhinal neurons showed that subthreshold membrane oscillation frequencies vary along the dorsal-ventral axis in a way corresponding to grid-field spacing, supporting cellular-physiology models of grid coding.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored by Lisa M. Giocomo, Eric A. Zilli, Erik Fransén and Michael E. Hasselmo; the primary paper lists Lisa M. Giocomo as first author.

sources.title: Temporal frequency of subthreshold oscillations scales with entorhinal grid cell field spacing.
sources.supports: Oscillation-frequency gradient, grid-field spacing relationship and Lisa M. Giocomo authorship.

contributions.value: Environmental boundaries correct accumulated grid-cell error
contributions.summary: Recordings during long rodent trajectories showed grid patterns accumulate coherent error with time and distance from the last boundary encounter, while boundary interactions correct error in a direction-dependent manner, implicating landmarks in grid stability.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Kiah Hardcastle and Surya Ganguli; the primary paper lists Lisa M. Giocomo as a coauthor.

sources.title: Environmental boundaries as an error correction mechanism for grid cells.
sources.supports: Boundary-dependent grid error correction and Lisa M. Giocomo authorship.

contributions.value: Rules for integrating landmark and self-motion cues in entorhinal navigation codes
contributions.summary: Virtual-reality recordings and modeling showed border cells track landmarks while grid and speed cells combine locomotion, optic flow and landmarks context-dependently, providing a framework for how entorhinal codes guide navigation.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Malcolm G. Campbell, Samuel A. Ocko, Caitlin S. Mallory and colleagues; the primary paper lists Lisa M. Giocomo as a coauthor.

sources.title: Principles governing the integration of landmark and self-motion cues in entorhinal cortical codes for navigation.
sources.supports: Cue-manipulation recordings, model framework and Lisa M. Giocomo authorship.

contributions.value: AGRP neurons rapidly orchestrate feeding behavior
contributions.summary: Cell-type-specific photostimulation showed that activating small numbers of AGRP neurons evokes rapid, selective feeding in mice, while POMC stimulation reduces intake through melanocortin signaling, establishing AGRP neurons as sufficient drivers of feeding circuits.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Yexica Aponte and Deniz Atasoy; the primary paper lists Scott M. Sternson as a coauthor.

contributions.value: PVH oxytocin-node circuit for AGRP-evoked hunger

contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Deniz Atasoy, J. Nicholas Betley and Helen H. Su; the primary paper lists Scott M. Sternson as a coauthor.

sources.title: Deconstruction of a neural circuit for hunger.

contributions.value: Need-sensing neurons as negative-valence teaching signals

contributions.attribution: Coauthored with J. Nicholas Betley, Shengjin Xu, Zhen Fang Huang Cao and colleagues; the primary paper lists Scott M. Sternson as a coauthor.

contributions.value: Hippocampal sequential experience replay during slow-wave sleep
contributions.summary: Recordings from rats running repeated place-cell sequences showed that the same ordered multi-neuron sequences recur in brief, temporally compressed bursts during subsequent slow-wave sleep, consistent with sleep-associated reactivation of sequential experience.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored by Albert K. Lee and Matthew A. Wilson; the updated candidate record lists Albert K. Lee as a full-name coauthor.

contributions.value: Whole-cell recordings from neurons in freely moving rats
contributions.summary: A miniature head-mounted stabilization method enabled long-duration whole-cell recordings from identified neurons in freely moving rats, linking intracellular membrane physiology with natural behavior rather than only immobilized preparations.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Ian D. Manns, Bert Sakmann and Michael Brecht; the updated candidate record lists Albert K. Lee as a full-name coauthor.

contributions.value: Sensory neural activity shapes cortical vascular networks
contributions.summary: Manipulating whisker-related activity in early postnatal mouse barrel cortex showed that neural activity is necessary and sufficient to alter vascular density and branching, linking sensory circuit activity to vascular patterning.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Baptiste Lacoste, Cesar H. Comin, Ayal Ben-Zvi and colleagues; the primary paper lists Chenghua Gu as a coauthor.

sources.title: Sensory-related neural activity regulates the structure of vascular networks in the cerebral cortex.
sources.supports: Activity-dependent vascular patterning and Chenghua Gu authorship.

contributions.value: Suppression of transcytosis governs blood-retinal barrier formation
contributions.summary: Mouse blood-retinal barrier studies showed that immature vessel leakage occurs through transcytosis despite early functional tight junctions, and that gradual developmental suppression of transcytosis determines barrier sealing.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Brian Wai Chow; the primary paper lists Chenghua Gu as a coauthor.

sources.title: Gradual Suppression of Transcytosis Governs Functional Blood-Retinal Barrier Formation.

contributions.value: Endothelial caveolae pathway in neurovascular coupling
contributions.summary: Two-photon imaging and genetic perturbations in awake mice showed that arteriolar endothelial caveolae provide a major nitric-oxide-independent pathway relaying neural activity to smooth muscle for local blood-flow increases.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Brian W. Chow, Vicente Nuñez, Luke Kaplan and colleagues; the primary paper lists Chenghua Gu as a coauthor.

records.name: Pietro De Camilli

identity.note: Imported roster identity; not independently established.

contribution_review.reason: Selected full-name synaptic-vesicle, membrane-fission and phase-separation primary papers.

contributions.value: Dynamin GTP-dependent twisting mechanism for membrane fission
contributions.summary: Real-time imaging of dynamin-coated lipid tubules showed GTP-dependent twisting and tension-associated breakage, supporting dynamin as a mechanoenzyme whose constriction cooperates with membrane tension during fission.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Aurélien Roux, Katherine Uyhazi and Adam Frost; the primary paper lists Pietro De Camilli as a coauthor.

sources.title: GTP-dependent twisting of dynamin implicates constriction and tension in membrane fission.
sources.supports: Dynamin twisting/fission mechanism and Pietro De Camilli authorship.

contributions.value: Activity-dependent requirement for dynamin 1 in synaptic vesicle endocytosis
contributions.summary: Dynamin-1 knockout synapses could function at baseline but accumulated tubular invaginations and failed during strong stimulation, showing that dynamin 1 is selectively required for efficient synaptic vesicle endocytosis under high activity.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Shawn M. Ferguson, Gabor Brasnjo, Mitsuko Hayashi and colleagues; the primary paper lists Pietro De Camilli as a coauthor.

sources.title: A selective activity-dependent requirement for dynamin 1 in synaptic vesicle endocytosis.
sources.supports: Activity-dependent dynamin 1 role in synaptic vesicle endocytosis and Pietro De Camilli authorship.

contributions.value: Synapsin liquid phase for synaptic vesicle clustering
contributions.summary: Biochemical reconstitution showed that synapsin forms a liquid phase that captures small lipid vesicles and disperses after phosphorylation, suggesting phase separation as a physical principle for synaptic vesicle clustering and release from reserve pools.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Dragomir Milovanovic, Yumei Wu and Xin Bian; the primary paper lists Pietro De Camilli as a coauthor.

sources.title: A liquid phase of synapsin and lipid vesicles.
sources.supports: Synapsin phase separation and Pietro De Camilli authorship.

contributions.summary: Transgenic mice expressing stabilized beta-catenin in neural precursors developed enlarged, folded cortices with expanded precursor populations, showing that beta-catenin can regulate cortical size by shifting proliferation versus differentiation.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Anjen Chenn; the primary paper lists Christopher A. Walsh as a coauthor.

contributions.value: Optogenetic reactivation of hippocampal engram cells evokes fear-memory recall
contributions.summary: In mice, neurons active during fear learning were tagged in the dentate gyrus and later reactivated in a different context; stimulation selectively induced freezing, supporting sufficiency of a sparse hippocampal ensemble for context-specific recall.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Xu Liu, Steve Ramirez, Petti T Pang, Corey B Puryear, Arvind Govindarajan, and Karl Deisseroth; the primary paper lists Susumu Tonegawa as a coauthor.

sources.title: Optogenetic stimulation of a hippocampal engram activates fear memory recall.

contributions.value: Prefrontal, hippocampal, and amygdala engrams reorganize during systems consolidation
contributions.summary: Mouse contextual fear-memory experiments showed that prefrontal engram cells are generated during initial learning, mature over time with hippocampal support, while hippocampal engrams become silent and amygdala engrams remain necessary for fear memory.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Takashi Kitamura, Sachie K Ogawa, Dheeraj S Roy, Teruhiro Okuyama, Mark D Morrissey, Lillian M Smith, and Roger L Redondo; the primary paper lists Susumu Tonegawa as a coauthor.

sources.title: Engrams and circuits crucial for systems consolidation of a memory.

contributions.value: Dentate gyrus NMDA receptors support hippocampal pattern separation
contributions.summary: A mouse strain lacking NR1 in dentate granule cells could learn contextual fear but was impaired at distinguishing similar contexts, with reduced CA3 context-specific modulation, linking dentate NMDA receptor function to pattern separation.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Thomas J McHugh, Matthew W Jones, Jennifer J Quinn, Nina Balthasar, Roberto Coppari, Joel K Elmquist, Bradford B Lowell, Michael S Fanselow, and Matthew A Wilson; the primary paper lists Susumu Tonegawa as a coauthor.

sources.title: Role of GABAergic inhibition in shaping odor-evoked spatiotemporal patterns in the Drosophila antennal lobe.

contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Shawn R Olsen and Vikas Bhandawat; the independently verified primary paper lists Rachel I Wilson as a coauthor.

sources.title: Divisive normalization in olfactory population codes.

contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Roozbeh Kiani; the primary paper lists Michael N Shadlen as a coauthor.

sources.title: Representation of confidence associated with a decision by neurons in the parietal cortex.

contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Arbora Resulaj, Roozbeh Kiani, and Daniel M Wolpert; the primary paper lists Michael N Shadlen as a coauthor.

sources.supports: Supports the behavioral evidence and model for post-decision reversals, with Michael N Shadlen coauthorship.

contributions.value: STORM localizes photoswitchable fluorophores for sub-diffraction fluorescence imaging
contributions.summary: The paper introduced stochastic optical reconstruction microscopy, reconstructing images from repeated sparse activation and localization of photoswitchable fluorophores, and demonstrated roughly 20-nanometer resolution in fluorescence imaging.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Michael J Rust and Mark Bates; the primary paper lists Xiaowei Zhuang as a coauthor.

sources.title: Sub-diffraction-limit imaging by stochastic optical reconstruction microscopy (STORM).
sources.supports: Supports the STORM imaging method, fluorophore-localization strategy, reported resolution, and Xiaowei Zhuang coauthorship.

contributions.value: MERFISH enables spatially resolved multiplexed RNA profiling in single cells
contributions.summary: MERFISH used error-robust single-molecule imaging codes to count and localize hundreds to thousands of RNA species in individual cells, enabling spatial transcriptome profiling and gene-correlation analyses.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Kok Hao Chen, Alistair N Boettiger, Jeffrey R Moffitt, and Siyuan Wang; the primary paper lists Xiaowei Zhuang as a coauthor.

sources.title: RNA imaging. Spatially resolved, highly multiplexed RNA profiling in single cells.

contributions.value: STORM revealed a periodic actin-spectrin cytoskeleton in axons
contributions.summary: Using STORM in neurons, the study found evenly spaced actin rings along axons, alternating spectrin organization, and coordinated periodic sodium-channel distribution, distinguishing axonal organization from dendritic actin filaments.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Ke Xu and Guisheng Zhong; the primary paper lists Xiaowei Zhuang as a coauthor.

sources.supports: Supports the discovery of periodic actin-spectrin organization in axons using STORM and Xiaowei Zhuang coauthorship.

contributions.value: Molecularly distinct interneurons form a complementary disinhibitory circuit motif
contributions.summary: In mouse visual cortex, parvalbumin interneurons mainly inhibited each other, somatostatin interneurons inhibited other populations while sparing themselves, and VIP interneurons preferentially inhibited somatostatin cells, outlining a layered inhibitory-circuit logic.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Carsten K Pfeffer, Mingshan Xue, Miao He, and Z Josh Huang; the primary paper lists Massimo Scanziani as a coauthor.

sources.title: Inhibition of inhibition in visual cortex: the logic of connections between molecularly distinct interneurons.
sources.supports: Supports the connectivity pattern among PV, SOM, and VIP interneurons and Massimo Scanziani coauthorship.

contributions.value: Parvalbumin-cell synapses equalize excitation-inhibition ratios across visual cortical neurons
contributions.summary: Recordings in mouse primary visual cortex showed that individual pyramidal cells receive inhibition proportional to their excitation, mediated by activity-dependent matching of parvalbumin-cell synapses rather than homogeneous inhibitory wiring.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Mingshan Xue and Bassam V Atallah; the primary paper lists Massimo Scanziani as a coauthor.

sources.title: Equalizing excitation-inhibition ratios across visual cortical neurons.
sources.supports: Supports matched excitation-inhibition ratios, PV-cell mediation, activity dependence, and Massimo Scanziani coauthorship.

contributions.value: Somatostatin interneurons mediate cortical surround suppression in visual cortex
contributions.summary: The study found that surround stimulation preferentially excites somatostatin interneurons through horizontal cortical axons, and perturbing these cells showed their contribution to suppressing pyramidal-cell responses to receptive-field center stimuli.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Hillel Adesnik, William Bruns, Hiroki Taniguchi, and Z Josh Huang; the primary paper lists Massimo Scanziani as a coauthor.

sources.title: A neural circuit for spatial summation in visual cortex.
sources.supports: Supports the SOM-cell circuit for surround suppression in mouse visual cortex and Massimo Scanziani coauthorship.

contributions.value: A tRNA-synthetase editing defect links translational infidelity to neurodegeneration
contributions.summary: The sticky mouse mutation compromised alanyl-tRNA synthetase proofreading, leading to mischarged tRNAs, accumulation of misfolded proteins, unfolded-protein responses, Purkinje cell loss, and ataxia.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Jeong Woong Lee, Kirk Beebe, Leslie A Nangle, Jaeseon Jang, Chantal M Longo-Guess, Stuart A Cook, Michael T Davisson, John P Sundberg, and Paul Schimmel; the primary paper lists Susan L Ackerman as a coauthor.

contributions.value: A CNS-specific tRNA mutation plus loss of ribosome rescue causes neurodegeneration
contributions.summary: In mice, loss of GTPBP2 in the presence of a central-nervous-system-expressed tRNA mutation caused ribosome stalling and widespread neurodegeneration, defining GTPBP2 as a ribosome rescue factor and exposing tRNA disease potential.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Ryuta Ishimura, Gabor Nagy, Ivan Dotu, Huihao Zhou, Xiang-Lei Yang, Paul Schimmel, Naohiro Senju, Yasuharu Nishimura, and Jeffrey H Chuang; the primary paper lists Susan L Ackerman as a coauthor.

contributions.value: SIL1 cochaperone disruption connects ER stress with Purkinje-cell neurodegeneration

contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Lihong Zhao, Chantal Longo-Guess, Belinda S Harris, and Jeong-Woong Lee; the primary paper lists Susan L Ackerman as a coauthor.

contributions.summary: Identified TRPA1/ANKTM1 as a sensory-neuron target for pungent irritants and showed in mutant mice that TRPA1 mediates responses to mustard oil, garlic-derived compounds, environmental irritants, and bradykinin-evoked pain hypersensitivity.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Sven-Eric Jordt, Diana M Bautista, and colleagues; PubMed author evidence lists Diana M Bautista as a coauthor. Credit is collaborative and does not imply sole authorship.

sources.title: Mustard oils and cannabinoids excite sensory nerve fibres through the TRP channel ANKTM1.
sources.supports: The paper identifies ANKTM1/TRPA1 activation by mustard oil and cannabinoids and lists Diana M. Bautista as a coauthor.

sources.title: TRPA1 mediates the inflammatory actions of environmental irritants and proalgesic agents.
sources.supports: The paper reports TRPA1-deficient mouse evidence for irritant and inflammatory pain signaling and lists Diana M. Bautista as a coauthor.

contributions.value: TRPM8 as a principal detector of environmental cold
contributions.summary: Showed that TRPM8-deficient sensory neurons, nerve fibers, and mice have strongly diminished cold responses, establishing TRPM8 as a predominant peripheral detector across a broad range of cool temperatures.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Diana M Bautista and colleagues; PubMed author evidence lists Diana M Bautista as a coauthor. Credit is collaborative and does not imply sole authorship.

sources.title: The menthol receptor TRPM8 is the principal detector of environmental cold.
sources.supports: The paper reports cellular, nerve, and behavioral evidence for TRPM8 in cold sensing and lists Diana M. Bautista as a coauthor.

contributions.value: Epithelial TSLP activation of sensory neurons to drive itch
contributions.summary: Showed that calcium-dependent TSLP release from keratinocytes can directly activate a subset of TRPA1-positive cutaneous sensory neurons, linking epithelial cytokine signaling to itch behaviors in atopic dermatitis models.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Sarah R Wilson and colleagues; PubMed author evidence lists Diana M Bautista as a coauthor. Credit is collaborative and does not imply sole authorship.

sources.title: The epithelial cell-derived atopic dermatitis cytokine TSLP activates neurons to induce itch.
sources.supports: The paper reports TSLP-dependent activation of sensory neurons and itch behavior and lists Diana M. Bautista as a coauthor.

contributions.value: Rats and humans can accumulate pulse evidence with little memory noise
contributions.summary: Behavioral tasks with randomly timed sensory pulses and trial-specific modeling separated incoming sensory noise from accumulator memory noise, showing that memory in the accumulation process was effectively noiseless in both rats and humans.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Bingni W Brunton and Matthew M Botvinick; the primary paper lists Carlos D Brody as a coauthor.

sources.title: Rats and humans can optimally accumulate evidence for decision-making.
sources.supports: Supports the pulse-evidence task, modeling separation of noise sources, rat and human findings, and Carlos D Brody coauthorship.

contributions.value: Parietal and frontal cortices encode evidence accumulation differently
contributions.summary: Recordings and causal silencing in rats found that posterior parietal cortex encoded graded accumulated evidence, while frontal orienting fields more categorically represented the provisional choice and affected behavior near decision commitment.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Timothy D Hanks, Charles D Kopec, Bingni W Brunton, Chunyu A Duan, and Jeffrey C Erlich; the primary paper lists Carlos D Brody as a coauthor.

sources.title: Distinct relationships of parietal and prefrontal cortices to evidence accumulation.
sources.supports: Supports distinct PPC and FOF relationships to accumulated evidence and Carlos D Brody coauthorship.

contributions.value: Posterior parietal cortex represents sensory history that biases behavior
contributions.summary: In an auditory parametric working-memory task, rat posterior parietal cortex carried more information about previous trials than current stimuli; silencing improved performance by reducing prior-stimulus effects on behavior.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Athena Akrami, Charles D Kopec, and Mathew E Diamond; the primary paper lists Carlos D Brody as a coauthor.

sources.title: Posterior parietal cortex represents sensory history and mediates its effects on behaviour.
sources.supports: Supports PPC coding of previous sensory stimuli, behavioral effect of silencing, and Carlos D Brody coauthorship.

contributions.value: Histone serotonylation marks permissive chromatin and enhances TFIID binding
contributions.summary: The paper identified H3 glutamine-5 serotonylation on H3K4me3-marked nucleosomes, found enrichment in serotonin-producing tissues such as brain and gut, and linked the combinatorial mark to permissive gene expression and differentiation.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Lorna A Farrelly, Robert E Thompson, Shuai Zhao, Ashley E Lepack, Yang Lyu, and colleagues; the primary paper lists Ian Maze as a coauthor.

sources.title: Histone serotonylation is a permissive modification that enhances TFIID binding to H3K4me3.
sources.supports: Supports identification of H3K4me3Q5ser, chromatin and transcriptional findings, and Ian Maze coauthorship.

contributions.value: Dorsal raphe histone serotonylation contributes to stress- and antidepressant-linked plasticity
contributions.summary: Mouse stress models and human MDD tissue analyses linked H3K4me3Q5ser dynamics in dorsal raphe nucleus to stress- and antidepressant-associated gene-expression patterns and depression-related behaviors.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Amni Al-Kachak, Giuseppina Di Salvo, Sasha L Fulton, Jennifer C Chan, Lorna A Farrelly, and colleagues; the primary paper lists Ian Maze as a coauthor.

contributions.value: Meningeal lymphatic function affects CNS waste clearance, aging, and Alzheimer-model pathology
contributions.summary: Mouse studies showed meningeal lymphatic vessels drain cerebrospinal and interstitial macromolecules to cervical lymph nodes; impaired lymphatic function slowed clearance, worsened cognition, and aggravated amyloid-β pathology in Alzheimer-model mice.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Sandro Da Mesquita, Antoine Louveau, Andrea Vaccari, Igor Smirnov, R Chase Cornelison, and colleagues; the primary paper lists Jonathan Kipnis as a coauthor.

sources.title: Functional aspects of meningeal lymphatics in ageing and Alzheimer's disease.
sources.supports: Supports meningeal lymphatic drainage, aging and Alzheimer-model findings, and Jonathan Kipnis coauthorship.

contributions.value: Skull and vertebral bone marrow supply myeloid cells to meninges and CNS borders
contributions.summary: The paper showed that mouse meninges receive monocytes and neutrophils from adjacent skull and vertebral bone marrow rather than only blood, and that border-derived myeloid cells can enter CNS tissue during injury and neuroinflammation.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Andrea Cugurra, Tornike Mamuladze, Justin Rustenhoven, Taitea Dykstra, Giorgi Beroshvili, and colleagues; the primary paper lists Jonathan Kipnis as a coauthor.

sources.title: Skull and vertebral bone marrow are myeloid cell reservoirs for the meninges and CNS parenchyma.
sources.supports: Supports adjacent bone-marrow myeloid reservoirs for CNS borders, injury/neuroinflammation findings, and Jonathan Kipnis coauthorship.

contributions.value: Arachnoid cuff exit points connect dura and brain for fluid and immune-cell exchange
contributions.summary: Transcriptomics, transgenic mice, and human imaging identified arachnoid cuff exit points at bridging veins as discontinuities that permit cerebrospinal-fluid and molecular exchange between subarachnoid space and dura and enable immune-cell entry during neuroinflammation.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Leon C D Smyth, Di Xu, Serhat V Okar, Taitea Dykstra, Justin Rustenhoven, and colleagues; the primary paper lists Jonathan Kipnis as a coauthor.

sources.title: Identification of direct connections between the dura and the brain.
sources.supports: Supports ACE-point anatomy, fluid/molecular exchange, neuroinflammatory trafficking, human imaging comparison, and Jonathan Kipnis coauthorship.

contributions.value: Plasma signaling-protein classification of Alzheimer's disease
contributions.summary: Identified a blood-plasma signaling-protein panel that classified Alzheimer's and control samples and flagged mild cognitive impairment cases that later progressed, linking the signal to systemic immune, hematopoietic and neuronal-support pathways.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored by Tony Wyss-Coray with Sandip Ray, Markus Britschgi and colleagues; the cited primary record(s) list Tony Wyss-Coray as a full-name coauthor.

sources.title: Classification and prediction of clinical Alzheimer's diagnosis based on plasma signaling proteins.
sources.supports: Reports an 18-protein plasma panel for Alzheimer's classification and future MCI progression; lists Tony Wyss-Coray as coauthor.

contributions.value: Clonally expanded CD8 T cells in Alzheimer's cerebrospinal fluid
contributions.summary: Showed adaptive immune changes in Alzheimer's disease, including expanded CD8 effector-memory cells in blood and clonally expanded antigen-experienced CD8 T cells patrolling cerebrospinal fluid.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored by Tony Wyss-Coray with David Gate, Naresha Saligrama and colleagues; the cited primary record(s) list Tony Wyss-Coray as a full-name coauthor.

sources.title: Clonally expanded CD8 T cells patrol the cerebrospinal fluid in Alzheimer's disease.
sources.supports: Reports blood and CSF adaptive immune signatures in Alzheimer's disease and clonal T-cell receptor evidence; lists Tony Wyss-Coray as coauthor.

contributions.value: Organ-specific aging signatures from the plasma proteome

contributions.attribution: Coauthored by Tony Wyss-Coray with Hamilton Se-Hwee Oh, Jarod Rutledge and colleagues; the cited primary record(s) list Tony Wyss-Coray as a full-name coauthor.

contributions.value: Classical complement and microglia in CNS synapse elimination
contributions.summary: Showed that classical complement proteins localize to developing CNS synapses and are required for normal synapse elimination, including anatomical refinement of retinogeniculate connections.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored by Ben A Barres with Beth Stevens, Nicola J Allen and colleagues; the cited primary record(s) list Ben A Barres as a full-name coauthor.

sources.title: The classical complement cascade mediates CNS synapse elimination.
sources.supports: Reports C1q/C3 requirement for developmental CNS synapse elimination; lists Ben A Barres as coauthor.

contributions.value: Microglia-induced neurotoxic reactive astrocytes
contributions.summary: Defined a reactive astrocyte subtype induced by activated microglia through IL-1α, TNF and C1q, showing these astrocytes lose supportive functions and can damage neurons and oligodendrocytes.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored by Ben A Barres with Shane A Liddelow, Kevin A Guttenplan and colleagues; the cited primary record(s) list Ben A Barres as a full-name coauthor.

sources.title: Neurotoxic reactive astrocytes are induced by activated microglia.
sources.supports: Reports induction and neurotoxic properties of A1 reactive astrocytes; lists Ben A Barres as coauthor.

contributions.value: RNA-seq transcriptome and splicing resource for CNS cell classes
contributions.summary: Created an RNA-seq resource for purified mouse cortical neurons, glial populations and vascular cells, enabling cell-type comparisons of gene expression and alternative splicing.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored by Ben A Barres with Ye Zhang, Kenian Chen and colleagues; the cited primary record(s) list Ben A Barres as a full-name coauthor.

sources.title: An RNA-sequencing transcriptome and splicing database of glia, neurons, and vascular cells of the cerebral cortex.

contribution_review.reason: Selected three full-name, neuroscience primary papers spanning cognitive control networks, developmental connectomics, and individual-level functional mapping.

contributions.value: Distinguished adaptive and stable human task-control networks
contributions.summary: Resting-state functional connectivity and graph analysis separated human control regions into a frontoparietal network linked to trial-by-trial start-cue and error adaptation and a cingulo-opercular network linked to sustained task-set maintenance.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Damien A. Fair, Francis M. Miezin, Alexander L. Cohen, Kristin K. Wenger, and colleagues; the primary paper lists Nico U. F. Dosenbach as first author.

sources.title: Distinct brain networks for adaptive and stable task control in humans.
sources.supports: Supports the two-network model of adaptive versus stable task control and Dosenbach's first-author role.

contributions.note: The source supports coauthored contribution to human fMRI network interpretation, not sole discovery.

contributions.value: Predicted individual brain maturity from resting functional connectivity
contributions.summary: A multivariate model used brief resting-state functional connectivity scans to estimate individual brain maturity across childhood through adulthood, with maturation linked especially to weakening short-range connections among major networks.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Binyam Nardos, Alexander L. Cohen, Damien A. Fair, Jonathan D. Power, and colleagues; the primary paper lists Nico U. F. Dosenbach as first author.

sources.title: Prediction of individual brain maturity using fMRI.
sources.supports: Supports the use of fcMRI and multivariate pattern analysis to predict individual developmental brain maturity and Dosenbach's first-author role.

contributions.note: The finding is bounded to typically developing participants and the reported fMRI model.

contributions.value: Built high-sampling precision maps of individual human functional connectomes
contributions.summary: A deeply sampled ten-person MRI dataset enabled high-fidelity, person-specific functional connectomes and showed individual network features and topologies that group averaging can obscure.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Evan M. Gordon, Timothy O. Laumann, Adrian W. Gilmore, Dillan J. Newbold, Deanna J. Greene, and colleagues; the primary paper lists Nico U. F. Dosenbach as a coauthor and last author.

sources.title: Precision Functional Mapping of Individual Human Brains.

contribution_review.reason: Selected full-name primary papers on cortical disinhibition, cholinergic reinforcement feedback, and confidence-related orbitofrontal function.

contributions.value: Defined VIP interneurons as cortical disinhibitory control elements
contributions.summary: In awake mice and cortical circuit preparations, VIP interneurons suppressed other inhibitory interneurons, were recruited by reward and punishment signals, and increased gain in a principal-cell subpopulation.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Hyun-Jae Pi, Balázs Hangya, Duda Kvitsiani, Joshua I. Sanders, and Z. Josh Huang; the primary paper lists Adam Kepecs as a coauthor and last author.

sources.title: Cortical interneurons that specialize in disinhibitory control.
sources.supports: Supports the VIP interneuron disinhibitory circuit finding and Kepecs's coauthor role.

contributions.note: The claim is limited to the studied mouse cortical areas and behavioral conditions.

contributions.value: Showed rapid reinforcement signaling by basal forebrain cholinergic neurons
contributions.summary: Identified cholinergic neurons in behaving mice and found that they respond rapidly and precisely to reward and punishment, scaling with reinforcement unexpectedness rather than trial-by-trial attention.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Balázs Hangya, Sachin P. Ranade, and Maja Lorenc; the primary paper lists Adam Kepecs as a coauthor and last author.

sources.title: Central Cholinergic Neurons Are Rapidly Recruited by Reinforcement Feedback.
sources.supports: Supports rapid reinforcement-related activity in identified cholinergic neurons and Kepecs's coauthor role.

contributions.note: The source does not generalize the signal to all cholinergic functions.

contributions.value: Linked orbitofrontal cortex to confidence-guided waiting decisions
contributions.summary: Using a postdecision waiting task in rats, the study found that orbitofrontal cortex inactivation disrupted confidence-based waiting without impairing perceptual decision accuracy, and a normative confidence model explained waiting times.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Armin Lak, Gil M. Costa, Erin Romberg, Alexei A. Koulakov, and Zachary F. Mainen; the primary paper lists Adam Kepecs as a coauthor and last author.

sources.title: Orbitofrontal cortex is required for optimal waiting based on decision confidence.
sources.supports: Supports the rat orbitofrontal cortex confidence-report finding and Kepecs's coauthor role.

contributions.note: The result is framed as an anatomical locus for one confidence report, not all metacognition.

contribution_review.reason: Selected full-name primary papers centered on TREM2-dependent microglial biology in neurodegeneration.

contributions.value: Connected TREM2 lipid sensing to microglial response in an Alzheimer's model
contributions.summary: In a mouse Alzheimer's model, TREM2 deficiency impaired microglial clustering around amyloid plaques and increased amyloid accumulation; the study also showed TREM2 recognition of damage-associated lipids and reduced lipid detection by the R47H risk variant.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Yaming Wang, Marina Cella, Kaitlin Mallinson, Jason D. Ulrich, Katherine L. Young, and colleagues; the primary paper lists Marco Colonna as a coauthor and last author.

sources.title: TREM2 lipid sensing sustains the microglial response in an Alzheimer's disease model.
sources.supports: Supports TREM2 lipid sensing, microglial plaque response findings, and Colonna's coauthor role.

contributions.note: The disease-mechanism claim is bounded to the reported model and ligand assays.

contributions.value: Showed TREM2 sustains microglial energetic and biosynthetic metabolism
contributions.summary: The study linked TREM2 deficiency or risk variants to abnormal autophagy and impaired mTOR-associated metabolic programs, supporting a model in which TREM2 maintains microglial fitness during Alzheimer's pathology.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Tyler K. Ulland, Wilbur M. Song, Stanley Ching-Cheng Huang, Jason D. Ulrich, Alexey Sergushichev, and colleagues; the primary paper lists Marco Colonna as a coauthor and last author.

contributions.value: Mapped TREM2-dependent and species-specific glial responses in Alzheimer's disease
contributions.summary: Single-nucleus transcriptomics in mouse and human Alzheimer's samples confirmed TREM2-dependent disease-associated microglia in mice, revealed reactive oligodendrocytes, and found human glial responses that differed substantially from mouse patterns.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Yingyue Zhou, Wilbur M. Song, Prabhakar S. Andhey, Amanda Swain, Tyler Levy, and colleagues; the primary paper lists Marco Colonna as a coauthor and last author.

contributions.value: Type 2 immune signaling in sensory neurons and chronic itch
contributions.summary: Linked type 2 cytokine signaling in sensory neurons to chronic itch, identifying neuronal IL-4 receptor and JAK1 pathways as components of neuroimmune communication rather than exclusively immune-cell signaling.

contributions.value: Basophil-neuronal signaling in acute itch flares
contributions.summary: Identified a basophil-leukotriene pathway engaging sensory neurons during acute itch flares in inflamed mouse skin, distinguishing this circuit from the mast cell-histamine pathway operating in steady-state conditions.
contributions.attribution: Brian S. Kim coauthored the study with Fang Wang, Anna M. Trier, Fengxian Li, Seonyoung Kim, and colleagues; the primary paper lists Kim as the last author.

contributions.value: Sensory-neuron support of lung immune homeostasis

contributions.value: Defined STAT3-dependent astroglial scar-border organization

contribution_review.reason: Selected full-name primary papers using human single-neuron recordings to study memory-guided choice, action cancellation, and performance monitoring.

contributions.value: Showed medial frontal cortex flexibly recruits memory-based choice representations
contributions.summary: Human single-neuron recordings showed that medial frontal cortex rapidly changed neural subspaces with task goals and selectively coordinated with hippocampal and amygdala field potentials when decisions required memory retrieval.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Juri Minxha, Ralph Adolphs, Stefano Fusi, and Adam N. Mamelak; the primary paper lists Ueli Rutishauser as a coauthor and last author.

sources.title: Flexible recruitment of memory-based choice representations by the human medial frontal cortex.
sources.supports: Supports flexible MFC memory-based choice representations and Rutishauser's coauthor role.

contributions.note: The study is based on recordings from neurosurgical human subjects.

contributions.value: Dissociated human subthalamic neurons for action selection and cancellation
contributions.summary: Recordings from human subthalamic nucleus found movement-related neurons and fast stop-signal neurons with distinct dorsal-ventral organization, indicating anatomically segregated signals for action selection and cancellation.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Clayton P. Mosher, Adam N. Mamelak, Mahsa Malekmohammadi, and Nader Pouratian; the primary paper lists Ueli Rutishauser as a coauthor and last author.

sources.title: Distinct roles of dorsal and ventral subthalamic neurons in action selection and cancellation.
sources.supports: Supports STN action selection/cancellation findings and Rutishauser's coauthor role.

contributions.note: The source distinguishes single-neuron signals from later beta-bursting events.

contributions.value: Resolved task-general and task-specific geometry of human medial frontal performance monitoring
contributions.summary: Single-neuron recordings during two conflict tasks showed intermixed medial frontal neurons encoding conflict probability, conflict, and error in a geometry that permitted both task specialization and abstract generalization.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Zhongzheng Fu, Danielle Beam, Jeffrey M. Chung, Chrystal M. Reed, Adam N. Mamelak, and Ralph Adolphs; the primary paper lists Ueli Rutishauser as a coauthor and last author.

contributions.value: Mapped DAF-16 downstream genes influencing C. elegans lifespan
contributions.summary: Expression profiling during early adulthood identified DAF-16-regulated genes downstream of insulin/IGF signaling, and functional testing indicated that many of these targets influence worm aging.

contributions.value: Connected HSF-1 and DAF-16 to longevity and protein aggregation protection
contributions.summary: The study showed that HSF-1 activity influences lifespan and works with DAF-16 to activate genes, including small heat-shock proteins, that promote longevity and delay polyglutamine-expansion protein aggregation in worms.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Ao-Lin Hsu and Cynthia Kenyon; the primary paper lists Coleen T. Murphy as a coauthor.

sources.title: Regulation of aging and age-related disease by DAF-16 and heat-shock factor.

contributions.value: Standardized C. elegans positive butanone learning and memory assays

contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Amanda Kauffman, Lance Parsons, Geneva Stein, Airon Wills, and Rachel Kaletsky; the primary paper lists Coleen Murphy as a coauthor and last author.

sources.title: C. elegans positive butanone learning, short-term, and long-term associative memory assays.

contributions.value: Defined reciprocal TGF-beta/IL-6 control of TH17 and regulatory T-cell differentiation
contributions.summary: Using Foxp3 reporter mice, the study showed that IL-6 blocks TGF-beta-induced regulatory T-cell generation and, together with TGF-beta, promotes pathogenic IL-17-producing T-helper cell differentiation.

contributions.value: Identified galectin-9 as a Tim-3 ligand that restrains TH1 immunity
contributions.summary: The study identified galectin-9 as a Tim-3 ligand and showed Tim-3-dependent effects on TH1 calcium flux, aggregation, death, and suppression of TH1 autoimmunity in vivo.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Chen Zhu, Ana C. Anderson, Anna Schubart, Huabao Xiong, Jaime Imitola, and colleagues; the primary paper lists Vijay K. Kuchroo as a coauthor and last author.

sources.title: The Tim-3 ligand galectin-9 negatively regulates T helper type 1 immunity.

contributions.value: Showed combined Tim-3 and PD-1 targeting can reverse tumor T-cell exhaustion
contributions.summary: In mouse solid tumors, Tim-3 and PD-1 coexpression marked severely exhausted CD8 tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes, and combined targeting of both pathways controlled tumor growth better than either pathway alone.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Kaori Sakuishi, Lionel Apetoh, Jenna M. Sullivan, Bruce R. Blazar, and Ana C. Anderson; the primary paper lists Vijay K. Kuchroo as a coauthor.

sources.title: Targeting Tim-3 and PD-1 pathways to reverse T cell exhaustion and restore anti-tumor immunity.
sources.supports: Supports combined Tim-3/PD-1 exhaustion targeting and Kuchroo's coauthor role.

contributions.note: The source is preclinical tumor-immunology work.

contributions.value: Quantified photon capture and signaling by melanopsin retinal ganglion cells
contributions.summary: The study measured intrinsic light responses of melanopsin retinal ganglion cells, finding low photon catch but large and prolonged responses capable of signaling single-photon absorption and influencing pupillary behavior.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Shin H. Kang, Tian Xue, Haining Zhong, Hsi-Wen Liao, Dwight E. Bergles, and King-Wai Yau; the primary paper lists Michael Tri H. Do as first author.

sources.title: Photon capture and signalling by melanopsin retinal ganglion cells.

contributions.note: The behavioral scope is non-image-forming light responses.

contributions.value: Showed melanopsin tristability supports sustained broadband phototransduction
contributions.summary: The paper provided evidence that light distributes melanopsin among two silent states and one signaling state, enabling pigment availability, sustained signal integration over time, and broad wavelength responsiveness in ipRGCs.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Alan Joseph Emanuel; the primary paper lists Michael Tri Hoang Do as a coauthor.

sources.title: Melanopsin tristability for sustained and broadband phototransduction.

contributions.summary: Large-scale single-cell RNA sequencing generated macaque foveal and peripheral retinal cell taxonomies, compared macaque and mouse retinal types, and mapped region- and type-specific expression of human retinal disease genes.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Yi-Rong Peng, Karthik Shekhar, Wenjun Yan, Dustin Herrmann, Anna Sappington, and colleagues; the primary paper lists Michael Tri H. Do as a coauthor.

contributions.value: Used single-cell RNA-seq to expose intratumoral glioblastoma heterogeneity
contributions.summary: Profiling individual cells from primary glioblastomas revealed variable transcriptional programs for oncogenic signaling, proliferation, immune response, hypoxia, and stemness, showing subtype classifiers vary within tumors.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Anoop P. Patel, Itay Tirosh, John J. Trombetta, Alex K. Shalek, Shawn M. Gillespie, and colleagues; the primary paper lists Mario L. Suvà as a coauthor.

sources.title: Single-cell RNA-seq highlights intratumoral heterogeneity in primary glioblastoma.

contributions.note: The source profiles five primary glioblastomas and does not define all glioblastoma biology.

contributions.value: Connected IDH-mutant glioma methylation to insulator loss and oncogene activation
contributions.summary: The study showed that IDH-mutant gliomas hypermethylate CTCF-binding sites, weakening chromatin insulation and enabling aberrant enhancer contact with PDGFRA, with demethylation or motif disruption experiments supporting causality.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with William A. Flavahan, Yotam Drier, Brian B. Liau, Shawn M. Gillespie, Andrew S. Venteicher, Anat O. Stemmer-Rachamimov, and Bradley E. Bernstein; the primary paper lists Mario L. Suvà as a coauthor.

contributions.note: The contribution is a glioma mechanism, not a treatment claim.

contributions.value: Built an integrated model of glioblastoma cellular states, plasticity, and genetics
contributions.summary: Combining single-cell RNA-seq, TCGA data, functional assays, and lineage tracing, the study defined four main malignant-cell states influenced by genetics and microenvironment and exhibiting plasticity.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Cyril Neftel, Julie Laffy, Mariella G. Filbin, Toshiro Hara, Marni E. Shore, and colleagues; the primary paper lists Mario L. Suvà as a coauthor and last author.

sources.title: An Integrative Model of Cellular States, Plasticity, and Genetics for Glioblastoma.

contributions.value: Showed epigenetic stability constrains exhausted T-cell reinvigoration after PD-1 blockade

contributions.value: Linked cytoplasmic chromatin to cGAS-STING inflammation in senescence and cancer

contributions.value: RGS complex rate-limits rod photoresponse recovery
contributions.summary: In mammalian rod photoreceptors, overexpressing the RGS9-1/Gbeta5L/R9AP complex accelerated light-response recovery whereas extra rhodopsin kinase did not, supporting G-protein deactivation as the limiting step for rod visual-transduction recovery.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Claudia M Krispel, Desheng Chen, Nathan Melling, and colleagues; the primary paper lists Kirill A Martemyanov as a coauthor.

sources.title: RGS expression rate-limits recovery of rod photoresponses.
sources.supports: Supports the rod-photoreceptor RGS overexpression finding, comparison with rhodopsin kinase, and Martemyanov authorship.

contributions.value: Optical profiling of GPCR coupling fingerprints across G proteins
contributions.summary: A single-platform live-cell optical strategy profiled how individual GPCRs activate different G-alpha subunits, revealing receptor-specific coupling fingerprints shaped by ligand class and intracellular signaling modulators.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Ikuo Masuho, Olga Ostrovskaya, Grant M Kramer, and colleagues; the primary paper lists Kirill A Martemyanov as a coauthor.

sources.title: Distinct profiles of functional discrimination among G proteins determine the actions of G protein-coupled receptors.
sources.supports: Supports the live-cell optical profiling platform, GPCR coupling fingerprints, ligand effects, and Martemyanov authorship.

contributions.value: Global map of RGS regulation of G-alpha signaling
contributions.summary: A systematic living-cell kinetic map of canonical human RGS proteins against G-alpha substrates defined selectivity rules, structural recognition principles, and effects of naturally occurring RGS variants on signaling.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Ikuo Masuho, Santhanam Balaji, Brian S Muntean, and colleagues; the primary paper lists Kirill A Martemyanov as a coauthor.

sources.title: A Global Map of G Protein Signaling Regulation by RGS Proteins.
sources.supports: Supports the global RGS-G-alpha activity map, selectivity rules, variant effects, and Martemyanov authorship.

contributions.value: APEX genetically encoded reporter for electron microscopy

contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Eric L Hargreaves, Geeta Rao, and Inah Lee; the primary paper lists James J Knierim as a coauthor.

sources.title: Major dissociation between medial and lateral entorhinal input to dorsal hippocampus.
sources.supports: Supports the entorhinal spatial/nonspatial dissociation and Knierim authorship.

contributions.value: Direct evidence for CA3 pattern completion and dentate pattern separation
contributions.summary: Simultaneous CA3 and dentate gyrus recordings during cue conflicts showed CA3 population outputs remained coherent with stored representations despite disrupted dentate inputs, supporting complementary pattern completion and separation in hippocampal memory processing.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Joshua P Neunuebel; the primary paper lists James J Knierim as a coauthor.

sources.title: CA3 retrieves coherent representations from degraded input: direct evidence for CA3 pattern completion and dentate gyrus pattern separation.
sources.supports: Supports CA3 pattern-completion and dentate pattern-separation findings and Knierim authorship.

contributions.value: Lateral entorhinal population coding of experienced time
contributions.summary: Population activity in lateral entorhinal cortex of freely foraging rats robustly encoded temporal information across seconds to hours, suggesting a route for integrating experienced time with hippocampal spatial representations.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Albert Tsao, Jørgen Sugar, Li Lu, and colleagues; the primary paper lists James J Knierim as a coauthor.

sources.title: Integrating time from experience in the lateral entorhinal cortex.
sources.supports: Supports lateral entorhinal time coding across behavioral timescales and Knierim authorship.

contributions.value: Spike-timing plasticity rules for natural spike trains
contributions.summary: Experiments in visual cortical slices showed that spike-timing-dependent synaptic modification during naturalistic spike trains depends on preceding spikes within each neuron, making the first spike in a burst especially influential.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Yang Dan; the primary paper lists Robert C Froemke as a coauthor.

sources.title: Spike-timing-dependent synaptic modification induced by natural spike trains.
sources.supports: Supports the natural-spike-train STDP findings and Froemke authorship.

contributions.value: Synaptic memory trace for auditory cortical receptive-field plasticity
contributions.summary: In vivo whole-cell recordings in adult auditory cortex revealed a rapid, stimulus-specific reduction in inhibition followed by persistent excitation and rebalanced inhibition after nucleus basalis pairing, providing a synaptic trace for receptive-field retuning.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Michael M Merzenich and Christoph E Schreiner; the primary paper lists Robert C Froemke as a coauthor.

sources.title: A synaptic memory trace for cortical receptive field plasticity.
sources.supports: Supports the auditory-cortical synaptic dynamics of receptive-field plasticity and Froemke authorship.

contributions.value: Oxytocin balancing cortical inhibition for maternal auditory behavior
contributions.summary: In female mice, oxytocin enhanced auditory cortical responses to pup calls and accelerated pup retrieval by balancing the timing and magnitude of inhibition with excitation, with lateralized involvement of left auditory cortex.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Bianca J Marlin, Mariela Mitre, James A D’amour, and Moses V Chao; the primary paper lists Robert C Froemke as a coauthor.

sources.title: Oxytocin enables maternal behaviour by balancing cortical inhibition.
sources.supports: Supports the oxytocin, auditory cortex, inhibitory-balance and pup-retrieval findings plus Froemke authorship.

contributions.value: BDNF requirement in mesolimbic social-defeat plasticity
contributions.summary: Pathway-specific BDNF knockdown in mice showed BDNF was required for social-defeat-induced social aversion and broad nucleus accumbens gene-expression changes, linking mesolimbic neurotrophic signaling to aversive social experience.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Olivier Berton, Colleen A McClung, Ralph J Dileone, and colleagues; the primary paper lists Eric J Nestler as a coauthor.

sources.title: Essential role of BDNF in the mesolimbic dopamine pathway in social defeat stress.
sources.supports: Supports the BDNF social-defeat findings and Nestler authorship.

contributions.value: Sustained hippocampal chromatin regulation in depression-model behavior
contributions.summary: Chronic social defeat in mice produced persistent Bdnf promoter repression and histone methylation in hippocampus, while chronic imipramine reversed expression changes through histone acetylation and HDAC5-linked mechanisms.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Nadia M Tsankova, Olivier Berton, William Renthal, and colleagues; the primary paper lists Eric J Nestler as a coauthor.

sources.title: Sustained hippocampal chromatin regulation in a mouse model of depression and antidepressant action.
sources.supports: Supports chromatin regulation of Bdnf in defeat stress and antidepressant action plus Nestler authorship.

contributions.value: Reward-circuit adaptations associated with social-defeat susceptibility and resilience
contributions.summary: Socially defeated mice separated into susceptible and unsusceptible subgroups with distinct behavioral, molecular and electrophysiological adaptations in mesolimbic reward circuitry; recapitulating several resilience-associated adaptations promoted resistant behavior.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Vaishnav Krishnan, Ming-Hu Han, Danielle L Graham, and colleagues; the primary paper lists Eric J Nestler as a coauthor.

sources.title: Molecular adaptations underlying susceptibility and resistance to social defeat in brain reward regions.
sources.supports: Supports the susceptibility/resilience stratification and reward-circuit adaptation findings plus Nestler authorship.

contributions.value: Neuron-type-specific reward and punishment signals in VTA
contributions.summary: Optogenetic tagging and recordings in mice showed VTA dopamine neurons carried reward-prediction-error-like signals, whereas VTA GABAergic neurons signaled expected reward, identifying complementary cell-type-specific variables.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Jeremiah Y Cohen, Sebastian Haesler, Linh Vong, and Bradford B Lowell; the primary paper lists Naoshige Uchida as a coauthor.

sources.title: Neuron-type-specific signals for reward and punishment in the ventral tegmental area.

contributions.value: Whole-brain monosynaptic input map to midbrain dopamine neurons
contributions.summary: Rabies-virus tracing comprehensively mapped direct inputs to VTA and substantia nigra dopamine neurons, revealing diverse and contrasting input sources that could help explain distinct dopamine-neuron signals.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Mitsuko Watabe-Uchida, Lisa Zhu, Sachie K Ogawa, and Archana Vamanrao; the primary paper lists Naoshige Uchida as a coauthor.

sources.title: Whole-brain mapping of direct inputs to midbrain dopamine neurons.

contributions.value: Local circuit subtraction underlying dopamine prediction errors
contributions.summary: Optogenetic manipulations during classical conditioning showed dopamine neurons perform a subtraction-like comparison of actual and expected reward, with neighboring VTA GABA neurons causally contributing expected-reward inhibition.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Neir Eshel, Michael Bukwich, Vinod Rao, and colleagues; the primary paper lists Naoshige Uchida as a coauthor.

sources.title: Arithmetic and local circuitry underlying dopamine prediction errors.
sources.supports: Supports dopamine prediction-error arithmetic and VTA GABA circuit mechanism plus Uchida authorship.

contribution_review.reason: Selected full-name primary papers on optogenetic tests of cortical gamma rhythms, excitation/inhibition balance, and prefrontal interneuron mechanisms.

contributions.value: Parvalbumin interneuron control of gamma rhythms and cortical performance
contributions.summary: Optogenetic manipulation in mice showed parvalbumin interneurons are necessary and sufficient for neocortical gamma rhythmicity, and that gamma-frequency modulation can improve cortical signal transmission by reducing noise and amplifying signals.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Feng Zhang, Ofer Yizhar, and Karl Deisseroth; the primary paper lists Vikaas S Sohal as a coauthor.

sources.title: Parvalbumin neurons and gamma rhythms enhance cortical circuit performance.

contributions.value: Causal test of elevated prefrontal excitation/inhibition balance in social dysfunction
contributions.summary: Optogenetic elevation of cellular excitation/inhibition balance in mouse medial prefrontal cortex impaired information processing and social behavior, while increasing inhibitory cell excitability partially rescued social deficits.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Ofer Yizhar, Lief E Fenno, Matthias Prigge, and colleagues; the primary paper lists Vikaas S Sohal as a coauthor.

sources.title: Neocortical excitation/inhibition balance in information processing and social dysfunction.
sources.supports: Supports the E/I-balance manipulation, social behavior effects, and Sohal authorship.

contributions.value: Prefrontal interneuron gamma rhythms restoring cognitive flexibility in mice
contributions.summary: In Dlx5/6 heterozygous mice, post-adolescent fast-spiking interneuron abnormalities coincided with deficient task-evoked gamma and cognitive inflexibility; gamma-frequency interneuron stimulation restored cognitive flexibility in adults.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Kathleen K A Cho, Renee Hoch, Anthony T Lee, and colleagues; the primary paper lists Vikaas S Sohal as a coauthor.

sources.title: Gamma rhythms link prefrontal interneuron dysfunction with cognitive inflexibility in Dlx5/6(+/-) mice.
sources.supports: Supports the interneuron/gamma/cognitive-flexibility mechanism and Sohal authorship.

contributions.value: Progranulin deficiency driving microglial complement-mediated synaptic pruning
contributions.summary: In progranulin-deficient mice, aging-associated microglial innate-immune activation increased complement production and selectively eliminated inhibitory synapses in ventral thalamus; C1qa deletion mitigated pruning, neurodegeneration and behavior.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Hansen Lui, Jiasheng Zhang, Stefanie R Makinson, and colleagues; the primary paper lists Eric J Huang as a coauthor.

sources.title: Progranulin Deficiency Promotes Circuit-Specific Synaptic Pruning by Microglia via Complement Activation.

contributions.value: Sharp developmental decline of human hippocampal neurogenesis

contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Shawn F Sorrells, Mercedes F Paredes, Arantxa Cebrian-Silla, and colleagues; the primary paper lists Eric J Huang as a coauthor.

sources.title: Human hippocampal neurogenesis drops sharply in children to undetectable levels in adults.

contributions.value: Optogenetic test of direct and indirect basal ganglia pathways in motor behavior

contributions.value: Clonal sequencing of adult neuronal genomes by reprogramming

contributions.value: Necrostatin-1 inhibition of necroptosis in ischemic injury

contributions.value: Genome-wide necroptosis signaling network
contributions.summary: A genome-wide siRNA screen identified hundreds of regulators of death-receptor-mediated necroptosis, including genes acting downstream of or regulating RIP1 kinase and factors separating necroptotic from apoptotic responses.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Junichi Hitomi, Dana E. Christofferson, Aylwin Ng and colleagues; the primary paper lists Junying Yuan as a coauthor.

contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Michael Boyce, Kevin F. Bryant, Céline Jousse and colleagues; the primary paper lists Junying Yuan as a coauthor.

contributions.value: Synaptotagmin 7 as a synaptic facilitation sensor
contributions.summary: The study showed that Syt7 is required for facilitation at multiple central synapses: knockout eliminated facilitation without altering initial release probability or residual calcium, and wild-type rescue restored the effect.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Skyler L. Jackman, Josef Turecek and Justine E. Belinsky; the primary paper lists Wade G. Regehr as a coauthor.

sources.title: The calcium sensor synaptotagmin 7 is required for synaptic facilitation.

contributions.value: Endocannabinoid control of cerebellar LTD induction
contributions.summary: This work linked Purkinje-cell endocannabinoid release to cerebellar LTD induction, showing requirements for CB1 receptors and 2-AG synthesis while distinguishing transient presynaptic inhibition from postsynaptic LTD expression.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Patrick K. Safo; the primary paper lists Wade G. Regehr as a coauthor.

sources.title: Endocannabinoids control the induction of cerebellar LTD.

contributions.value: Mouse cerebellar cortex transcriptomic cell atlas
contributions.summary: High-throughput transcriptional profiling across adult mouse cerebellar lobules defined cerebellar cell types, revealing regional Purkinje specialization, continuous interneuron variation, and functionally distinct molecular-layer interneuron classes.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Velina Kozareva, Caroline Martin, Tomas Osorno and colleagues; the primary paper lists Wade G. Regehr as a coauthor.

sources.title: A transcriptomic atlas of mouse cerebellar cortex comprehensively defines cell types.
sources.supports: Supports the cerebellar cell-atlas resource and Regehr's authorship.

contributions.value: Glial netrin signaling for local synaptogenesis
contributions.summary: In C. elegans, glial UNC-6/netrin guided RIA outgrowth and locally promoted AIY presynaptic assembly through UNC-40/DCC, showing how glia can act as guideposts for circuit assembly in vivo.

contributions.value: Synaptic glycolytic metabolon under energy stress
contributions.summary: The paper reported that energy stress drives glycolytic enzymes to assemble near C. elegans synapses in a presynaptic-scaffold-dependent compartment that maintains local ATP, supports vesicle cycling, and affects locomotion.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with SoRi Jang, Jessica C. Nelson, Eric G. Bend and colleagues; the primary paper lists Daniel A. Colón-Ramos as a coauthor.

sources.title: Glycolytic Enzymes Localize to Synapses under Energy Stress to Support Synaptic Function.

contributions.value: KIF1A/UNC-104 transport of ATG-9 for synaptic autophagy

contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Andrea K. H. Stavoe, Sarah E. Kargbo-Hill and David H. Hall; the primary paper lists Daniel A. Colón-Ramos as a coauthor.

sources.title: KIF1A/UNC-104 Transports ATG-9 to Regulate Neurodevelopment and Autophagy at Synapses.
sources.supports: Supports the KIF1A/ATG-9 autophagy finding and Colón-Ramos's authorship.

sources.title: Coding of odors by a receptor repertoire.

contributions.value: Retinal waves coordinate developing visual-system activity

contributions.attribution: Coauthored with James B. Ackman and Timothy J. Burbridge; the primary paper lists Michael C. Crair as a coauthor.

sources.title: Retinal waves coordinate patterned activity throughout the developing visual system.

contributions.value: Patterned spontaneous activity instructs visual map development

contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Hong-ping Xu, Moran Furman, Yann S. Mineur and colleagues; the primary paper lists Michael C. Crair as a coauthor.

sources.title: An instructive role for patterned spontaneous retinal activity in mouse visual map development.

contributions.value: Simultaneous cortex-wide calcium imaging and whole-brain fMRI

sources.title: Simultaneous cortex-wide fluorescence Ca 2+ imaging and whole-brain fMRI.

records.name: Marcelo Dietrich

identity.note: Imported roster identity; not independently established.

contribution_review.reason: Selected full-name primary papers on hypothalamic metabolism, mitochondrial-ER control, and glial leptin signaling.

contributions.value: MFN2 control of POMC-neuron leptin sensitivity
contributions.summary: The paper connected reduced mitochondria-ER contacts in hypothalamic POMC neurons to diet-induced obesity, showing that POMC-specific Mfn2 loss caused ER stress, leptin resistance, hyperphagia, and reduced energy expenditure in mice.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Marc Schneeberger, David Sebastián, Mónica Imbernón and colleagues; the primary paper lists Marcelo O. Dietrich as a coauthor.

sources.title: Mitofusin 2 in POMC neurons connects ER stress with leptin resistance and energy imbalance.

contributions.value: POMC neurons in cannabinoid-induced feeding
contributions.summary: This study found that CB1 receptor activation paradoxically increases POMC neuronal activity and selectively promotes β-endorphin release, with POMC activity and opioid signaling required for acute cannabinoid-induced feeding in mice.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Marco Koch, Luis Varela, Jae Geun Kim and colleagues; the primary paper lists Marcelo O. Dietrich as a coauthor.

sources.title: Hypothalamic POMC neurons promote cannabinoid-induced feeding.
sources.supports: Supports the POMC cannabinoid-feeding finding and Dietrich's authorship.

contributions.value: Astrocyte leptin signaling in feeding circuits
contributions.summary: Conditional deletion of leptin receptors from hypothalamic astrocytes altered glial morphology and synaptic inputs onto feeding-related neurons, reducing leptin-regulated feeding while elevating fasting- or ghrelin-evoked feeding responses.
contributions.attribution: Coauthored with Jae Geun Kim, Shigetomo Suyama, Marco Koch and colleagues; the primary paper lists Marcelo O. Dietrich as a coauthor.

sources.title: Leptin signaling in astrocytes regulates hypothalamic neuronal circuits and feeding.
sources.supports: Supports the astrocyte leptin-circuit finding and Dietrich's authorship.
